format: html
execute:
  echo: true

## Learning goals

By the end of this exercise, you should be able to:

- compare alternative phenotype definitions;
- investigate disagreement between registry and chart review;
- conduct simple sensitivity analyses;
- document a transparent phenotype protocol.

## Load data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

review <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "emr_review.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

notes <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "emr_notes_excerpt.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

diagnoses <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "registry_diagnoses.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

contacts <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "registry_contacts.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

procedures <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "procedures.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## Task 1: Investigate discordant cases

Focus on:

```{r}
discordant_people <- c(
  "P002",
  "P003",
  "P004",
  "P006",
  "P010",
  "P016",
  "P017"
)

review |> 
  filter(person_id %in% discordant_people)
```

```{r}
notes |> 
  filter(person_id %in% discordant_people)
```

```{r}
diagnoses |> 
  filter(person_id %in% discordant_people)
```

```{r}
contacts |> 
  filter(person_id %in% discordant_people)
```

```{r}
procedures |> 
  filter(person_id %in% discordant_people)
```

For each participant, discuss:

1. Does the registry identify IHD?
2. Does chart review identify IHD?
3. Why might the sources disagree?
4. Is the disagreement caused by coding, timing, clinical uncertainty, historical disease, or incomplete data?
5. Would a different phenotype algorithm change the classification?

## Task 2: Sensitivity analyses

Compare the following algorithms:

1. Any ICD-10 or ICD-9 IHD code.
2. Inpatient primary IHD diagnosis only.
3. At least two outpatient IHD contacts.
4. Inpatient primary IHD diagnosis OR repeated outpatient IHD contacts.
5. Registry diagnosis plus coronary procedure.

For each algorithm, report:

| Algorithm | Number of cases | PPV | Main concern |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Broad | | | |
| Inpatient primary only | | | |
| Repeated outpatient only | | | |
| Combined strict algorithm | | | |
| Diagnosis plus procedure | | | |

## Task 3: Complete a phenotype protocol

Open:

```text
data/dictionary/phenotype_protocol_template.md
```

Complete the following sections:

- target condition;
- data sources;
- ICD and SNOMED concepts;
- included and excluded codes;
- inpatient/outpatient rules;
- primary/secondary diagnosis rules;
- date rule;
- prevalent IHD rule;
- first-event rule;
- validation strategy;
- sensitivity analyses;
- limitations.

## Final reflection

Discuss the following statements:

1. “A registry code is a diagnosis.”
2. “A chart review is always a perfect reference standard.”
3. “A stricter phenotype is always better.”
4. “A standard terminology solves interoperability problems.”
5. “The same registry can give different answers depending on the phenotype definition.”

Write a short group conclusion:

> Our preferred phenotype is __________ because __________.  
> Its most important limitation is __________.
